question: Should you be baptized?
summary: Matthew 28:19 places baptism at the center of the risen Jesus' Great Commission to the eleven — go, make disciples, baptize them in the triune name. Paul in 1 Corinthians 1:14, 17 says the opposite about his own mission — he thanks God he baptized almost no one in Corinth, and flatly states that Christ did not send him to baptize but to preach the gospel. The contradiction is at the level of mission priority: Matthew's Jesus makes baptism constitutive of the commission; Paul explicitly excludes it from his own.

reconcile.connective: Matthew Henry answers his own question directly: Paul delegated the rite to co-workers so he could give himself to preaching, not because he slighted the commission to baptize.

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman argues the trinitarian baptismal formula in Matthew 28:19 reflects the liturgical practice of Matthew's own community decades after Jesus, not a command the historical Jesus gave or Paul would have known.

pd_work.note: Haley's 'Baptism' section (p. 257) sets Matt 28:19 against 1 Cor 1:14, 17 verbatim under 'Enjoined' / 'Neglected' headings and reconciles them: 'Christ sent me not so much to baptize, as to preach the gospel. Paul did not neglect or undervalue baptism, but gave himself to the work of teaching, leaving his associates to administer baptism.'

excerpts.attribution: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible (1706-14)
excerpts.excerpt_text: Was it not a part of the apostolical commission to baptize all nations? And could Paul give thanks to God for his own neglect of duty? He is not to be understood in such a sense as if he were thankful for not having baptized at all, but for not having done it in present circumstances, lest it should have had this very bad construction put upon it - that he had baptized in his own name, made disciples for himself, or set himself up as the head of a sect. He left it to other ministers to baptize, while he set himself to more useful work, and filled up his time with preaching the gospel. This, he thought, was more his business, because the more important business of the two. … In this sense he says, Christ sent him not to baptize, but to preach the gospel - not so much to baptize as to preach.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Henry names the exact objection (Matt 28:19's commission to baptize all nations) and answers it: Paul's thanksgiving is about delegation of the rite, not devaluation of the commission, resolving the mission-priority tension the row turns on.
excerpts.source_note_text: Here the apostle gives an account of his ministry among them. He thanks God he had baptized but a few among them, Crispus, who had been a ruler of a synagogue at Corinth (Act 18:8), Gaius, and the household of Stephanas, besides whom, he says, he did not remember that he had baptized any. But how was this a proper matter for thankfulness? Was it not a part of the apostolical commission to baptize all nations? And could Paul give thanks to God for his own neglect of duty? He is not to be understood in such a sense as if he were thankful for not having baptized at all, but for not having done it in present circumstances, lest it should have had this very bad construction put upon it - that he had baptized in his own name, made disciples for himself, or set himself up as the head of a sect. He left it to other ministers to baptize, while he set himself to more useful work, and filled up his time with preaching the gospel. This, he thought, was more his business, because the more important business of the two. He had assistants that could baptize, when none could discharge the other part of his office so well as himself. In this sense he says, Christ sent him not to baptize, but to preach the gospel - not so much to baptize as to preach. Note, Ministers should consider themselves sent and set apart more especially to that service in which Christ will be most honoured and the salvation of souls promoted, and for which they are best fitted, though no part of their duty is to be neglected. The principal business Paul did among them was to preach the gospel (Co1 1:17), the cross (Co1 1:18), Christ crucified, Co1 1:23. Ministers are the soldiers of Christ, and are to erect and display the banner of the cross. He did not preach his own fancy, but the gospel - the glad tidings of peace, and reconciliation to God, through the mediation of a crucified Redeemer. This is the sum and substance of the gospel. Christ crucified is the foundation of all our joys. By his death we live. This is what Paul preached, what all ministers should preach, and what all the saints live upon.
